answer: Price identity in RAM that cannot be shared, not in elapsed time. Each mint must evaluate a memory-hard function over a large buffer, a lotus of pseudo-random lookups across gigabytes, held resident the whole epoch. Time-memory tradeoffs are blocked, so cost cannot be amortized: one host fronting a lagoon of personas must allocate a full buffer per identity at once, and the shared hardware bridges none of it between them. A thousand fakes need a thousand simultaneous buffers; physical memory is the scarce gate that caps fleet size at linear cost per head.
